description.text: The promos of the HeartGold & SoulSilver Series, HGSS01 to HGSS25, released from February 2010 to February 2011, when the promo prefix changed from DP to HGSS. Ho-Oh and Lugia came in poster packs and the Knock Out Collection; the Johto first partners in spring 2010 collector's tins and the legendary beasts Raikou, Entei and Suicune in the fall tins; the rest in blisters of each expansion through Call of Legends. Latias and Latios came both in cosmos holo and in cracked ice holo, and the trophy card Tropical Tidal Wave went to players at the 2010 World Championships.

description.text:
A holofoil Pikachu from the HeartGold & SoulSilver three-pack blister, released with the set on 10 February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Legends Awakened pack and a coin. The other blister held Wobbuffet HGSS04. Pikachu came back once the Black & White series had begun, in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Variety Blister, which held three random older booster packs.

Kanako Eo's art first came in Japan as a Gold Rank prize of the Pokémon Daisuki Club, for members who had collected 1,200 Action Points: first as 016/DPt-P, then reprinted as 019/L-P when the card game moved into the LEGEND era. Its Weakness reads +10 instead of ×2, making it the only HeartGold & SoulSilver series card with an added-damage Weakness and the last new English card to have one.

description.text:
A holofoil Raikou in its shiny colors from the 2010 fall Collector's Tins, sold from September 2010. Each tin held its shiny promo, a cracked ice holofoil reprint of the same Pokémon's Secret Wonders card to show the difference, and one pack each of Undaunted, HeartGold & SoulSilver, the Platinum series and the Diamond & Pearl series. The other tins held Entei HGSS20 and Suicune HGSS21, and a note inside promised more shiny Pokémon in future sets.

Noriko Hotta's art first came in Japan as Raikou 061/L-P in the LEGEND Perfect Set, released with the film Zoroark: Master of Illusions on 10 July 2010. The card matches the shiny Raikou that Japanese players could get for their games as a promotion for the film: its only attack, Zap Cannon, is the special move that Raikou knew.
